text:
Noah: Quick docs bug I noticed: our rate limit examples show response headers as strings in the curl samples (e.g. `X-RateLimit-Limit: "100"`) while the runtime and SDKs treat them as integers. This trips people when they parse headers and get a string with quotes.

Pri: Hmm. How did the quotes get in there? That sounds like an accidental copy from an HTTP inspector.

Noah: Exactly. The OpenAPI example response in /status currently lists headers as `"100"` in several example blocks. SDK snippets then demonstrate parsing as ints, which makes the mismatch worse.

Avery: I ran into a support ticket where a customer wrote `parseInt(headers['X-RateLimit-Limit'])` and it returned NaN because the header value had extra quotes. We should standardize examples to show numeric headers without quotes and add a tiny note about proxies that sometimes stringify headers.

Pri: Agreed. Proposed changes: 1) Update OpenAPI example responses to show numeric header values like `100` (no quotes). 2) Update curl/python/js snippets to display raw numeric headers and parsing examples. 3) Add a short migration comment: "If you see quoted header values (e.g. \"100\"), strip quotes before parsing; some proxies can stringify header values." 4) Add a docs-e2e lint to fail if any `X-RateLimit-` example matches `".*"`.

Noah: Also watch the Go SDK example: there's a snippet using `strconv.Atoi` directly on the header value which will error with quotes. We should change the snippet to a safe parser that trims quotes first.

Avery: I'll draft the safe parser in Go and JS for code samples. JS: `Number(headers['X-RateLimit-Limit']?.replace(/^\"|\"$/g, ''))` and Go: `strings.Trim(h, "\"")` then `strconv.Atoi`. Keep examples defensive.

Pri: Good. Can you include a one-line note in the reference response example: "Header values are integers; if your client sees quoted strings, trim quotes before parsing." That should reduce noisy issues.

Avery: Will do. I'll also add a docs lint rule that searches examples for `X-RateLimit-` and rejects if value contains leading/trailing quote char in the OpenAPI YAML.

docs-bot: Created issue #2205 and opened draft PR #3187 with OpenAPI example fixes, updated SDK snippets, and a docs-e2e lint: https://git.redwood/g/infra/docs/pulls/3187

Noah: Thanks. Pri, can you review the PR when it's ready? I want to ensure we don't accidentally change any real header schemas (this is purely example cleanup).

Pri: Yup, will review after CI runs. Thanks for catching this ":thumbsup:"
